therapeutic_hypothesis.claimed_target: prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP) and androgen receptor
therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: autologous antigen presenting cells loaded with PAP-GM-CSF fusion protein to stimulate immune response, combined with androgen receptor inhibition
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: T-cell mediated immune response against prostate cancer antigens and androgen receptor signaling blockade
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: men with metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: peripheral PA2024-specific T cell proliferation response via stimulation index

results.effect_size: p = 0.095 for mixed models analysis comparing concurrent vs sequential arms
results.target_engagement_evidence: T-cell proliferation responses observed in both arms with higher responses in concurrent arm at most timepoints
biomarker_changes: PA2024-specific T cell proliferation increased from baseline in both arms
Concurrent arm showed higher stimulation index values at most timepoints
subgroup_findings: Concurrent arm had consistently higher T-cell responses through week 40
Sequential arm showed higher response at week 52
results.dose_information: sipuleucel-T per standard protocol, enzalutamide 160 mg orally once daily

context.comparator: concurrent vs sequential administration of sipuleucel-T with enzalutamide
context.duration: 52 weeks follow-up after first sipuleucel-T dose
